headline: Five IGNIS + engagement improvements that reduce oracle friction and convert returning visitors, plus two structural gates that close a deploy-verification gap and an OG-image lying-surface class.

candidates.title: IGNIS contextual query suggestions — pre-populate Oracle with page-aware queries
candidates.why: When a visitor opens the Oracle panel from /games/, /membership/, or /universe/voidfall/, the empty search box is a conversion dead-end — they must already know what to ask. Pre-populating 3 context-relevant query chips (e.g. on /games/: 'What games are in development?', 'How do I earn Vault Rank?') gives the visitor an immediate reason to engage. The ?q= URL pre-fill is already wired (ignis-answer-engine.js:578) and works end-to-end — this is a pure JS enhancement that routes through existing infrastructure.
candidates.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js, detect window.location.pathname on boot(). Map known paths to 3 query chips: /games/* → game queries, /membership/* → tier/rank queries, /universe/* → lore queries, /oracle/ → leave empty (user came to search). Render chips in .vs-ignis-header as clickable pills that call query() via the ?q= pre-fill path. Style via ensureStyles() (style-contract compliant — no inline style=).
candidates.evidence: ignis-answer-engine.js:574–578 — ?q= URL pre-fill already works; ignis-answer-engine.js:150–152 — ensureStyles() pattern established; no current page-context detection exists (grep 'pathname' → 0 hits in ignis-answer-engine.js).

L1.recipe: Static page→3-query map, chips injected into the Oracle header on oracle.html + inline on non-oracle pages.

L2.recipe: URL pattern detection (pathname.startsWith) + chip render via ensureStyles(); RUM event oracle:suggestion_click for each chip.

L3.recipe: Personalized suggestions from world_affinity (home-personalized.js) + ignis_prefix_cache history — surfaces the query most likely to answer the user's current journey-stage question.

candidates.premiseEvidence: grep 'URLSearchParams' ignis-answer-engine.js:290,578 confirms ?q= wiring; grep 'pathname' → 0 hits confirms no context detection today

candidates.title: Returning-visitor 'What sparked since you left' signal strip
candidates.why: Visitors with vs_visit_count >= 2 already see personalized copy in home-personalized.js (cadence bucket: 'Welcome back') but that script is intentionally disabled on / (the bare homepage is identical for everyone). Non-homepage returning visitors get warm copy but no 'what changed' momentum signal. api/changelog-narrative.json (12KB, byWeek structure, S205-shipped, voice-driven entries) has exactly this content — shipping it as a slim 'N sessions since your last visit — here's what sparked' strip turns a return visit into a subscribe moment. Conversion outcome: visitor leaves with a reason to return sooner.
candidates.recipe: New asset: assets/returning-signal-strip.js. Reads localStorage vs_last_visit_ts + vs_visit_count (already set by ambient-loader). If visit_count >= 2, fetches api/changelog-narrative.json and finds entries newer than vs_last_visit_ts. Renders a dismissible top-of-content strip with 1-2 changelog headlines + 'See full changelog' CTA to /changelog/. RUM: signal:strip_shown, signal:strip_dismissed, signal:strip_cta. Predicate-loaded (returning-visitor only) via ambient-loader.
candidates.evidence: assets/ambient-loader.js:59 — vs_visit_count already tracked; api/changelog-narrative.json: 12225 bytes, byWeek structure (ls -la confirms fresh 2026-06-19); home-personalized.js explicitly returns early on /. No current 'what changed' surface exists for returning visitors.

L1.recipe: Static 'X new sessions since your last visit' count from vs_last_session_count diff. No API fetch.

L2.recipe: Fetch changelog-narrative.json, filter byWeek since vs_last_visit_ts, render up to 2 human-voice headlines in a dismissible strip.

L3.recipe: Full delta from public-intelligence.json: new projects, status changes, game milestones since last visit. Cross-reference vs_world_affinity to surface only relevant updates (new DreadSpike content → surface to DreadSpike-affinity visitors only).

candidates.premiseEvidence: ambient-loader.js:59 vs_visit_count confirmed; api/changelog-narrative.json confirmed present and fresh; home-personalized.js:7-8 returns early on /

candidates.title: Post-push CF Pages build verification — confirm the right SHA deployed
candidates.why: The closeout-autopilot already verifies that origin/main ref advanced after push (scripts/closeout-autopilot.mjs:339-342), preventing the S184 ref-movement gap. But it does NOT verify that CF Pages actually built from that SHA — a [skip ci] tip guard (check-deploy-tip.mjs) prevents strand risk, but doesn't confirm the build landed. The genius hit list at #96 calls this out: 'complete once the rem[ote build confirms].' A probe of vaultsparkstudios-website.pages.dev that reads a build-time stamp file or API response gives genuine deploy confidence. Conversion outcome: zero phantom-green closeouts where prod silently lags.
candidates.recipe: Extend scripts/closeout-autopilot.mjs Step 7 (after push verify). Add check-pages-deploy.mjs: fetches https://vaultsparkstudios-website.pages.dev/api/build-manifest.json (or any tiny file that changes every build). If the response body contains the pushed HEAD SHA (embed it at build time in a dedicated /api/build-sha.json → echo HEAD SHA in npm run build), the deploy is confirmed. If probe returns prior SHA or fails: log advisory + write context/.deploy-pending with SHA. Next session /start checks and surfaces pending deploy. Honest-dark: no false-green.
candidates.evidence: scripts/closeout-autopilot.mjs:339 — ref-verify exists; scripts/check-deploy-tip.mjs confirmed present; scripts/prod-verify-wave.mjs confirmed present but verifies wave surfaces not SHA; grep 'build-sha\.json' → 0 hits confirms gap

L1.recipe: Add /api/build-sha.json (echo git SHA > api/build-sha.json in npm run build). Log the file path — confirms the build system runs the script.

L2.recipe: check-pages-deploy.mjs probes pages.dev/api/build-sha.json, compares to pushed HEAD SHA, writes .deploy-pending advisory if mismatch. Wire into closeout-autopilot after push.

L3.recipe: Wire CF Pages API (via cloudflare.deploy credential) to check actual deployment status of the pushed SHA, not just the file content. Surface build duration + status tile on /status/.

candidates.premiseEvidence: closeout-autopilot.mjs:339 confirms ref-verify exists but not CF Pages build verify; check-deploy-tip.mjs present; grep 'build-sha' returns 0 hits

candidates.title: IGNIS 'Searching the Forge' loading trust animation
candidates.why: Cold IGNIS queries show a blank panel while fetching (line 48 silently loads, no DOM update). The prefix cache at line 180 gives continuity on cache hits only — 0 feedback for cold queries. A 'Searching 44,691 FORGE units…' animated message (advancing doc-count from 0 to the real count over 1.5s, read from api/public-intelligence.json metadata) transforms a frustrating white box into a trust-building intelligence signal. The count grounds the oracle's capability in visible scale. Conversion outcome: reduces cold-query abandonment.
candidates.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js boot(), when a search fires: (1) immediately show .vs-ignis-answer with a loading div — text 'Searching N FORGE units…' where N is pulled from indexPromise metadata or a cached constant; (2) animate a numeric count from 0 to N over 1.2s via requestAnimationFrame; (3) replace with results when the promise resolves. Use ensureStyles() for the loading div (style-contract compliant). Doc count: read from the public-intelligence.json totalDocuments field already fetched at line 414.
candidates.evidence: ignis-answer-engine.js:48 — fetch with empty .catch; line 180 — prefix cache hit only; line 414 — public-intelligence.json already fetched; grep 'Searching\|loading.*text' → 0 hits in ignis-answer-engine.js

L1.recipe: Static 'Searching the Forge…' text in the loading state, no count animation.

L2.recipe: Animated count 0→N from public-intelligence.json totalDocuments over 1.2s via rAF.

L3.recipe: Phase-aware messages: 'Scanning…' (0-400ms) → 'Ranking by relevance…' (400-800ms) → 'Assembling answer…' (800ms-done) with a thin progress bar. Cancels if result arrives early.

candidates.premiseEvidence: ignis-answer-engine.js:48 confirmed empty catch (silent); grep 'Searching' → 0 hits; line 414 public-intelligence fetch confirmed reachable

candidates.title: IGNIS offline fallback — show cached prior answers on network error
candidates.why: ignis-answer-engine.js:48 — on network error, fetch returns { documents: [] } silently and the user sees no answer and no explanation. vs_ignis_prefix_cache (20-entry LRU, 24h TTL, S206 shipped) already holds up to 20 prior answer excerpts from recent queries — but is never used in the error path. Surfacing the last 5 cached answers as a 'From your last Forge session' accordion when the network fails turns a dead-end into a useful fallback. SOUL-aligned: the vault never leaves you empty-handed.
candidates.recipe: In ignis-answer-engine.js, modify the catch handler at line 48 to: (1) read vs_ignis_prefix_cache from localStorage; (2) if non-empty, render a '.vs-ignis-offline-panel' with the top 5 cached query→excerpt pairs labeled 'Cached — network unavailable'; (3) show a 'Try again' retry link. Via ensureStyles() CSS only. RUM: oracle:offline_cache_shown. Conversion outcome: retains oracle engagement through network hiccups.
candidates.evidence: ignis-answer-engine.js:48 catch returns {documents:[]} silently; ignis-answer-engine.js:180 confirms prefix_cache is already read on cache hits; grep 'vs_ignis_prefix_cache' confirms it exists in localStorage writes

L1.recipe: Show 'Network unavailable — try again' with a retry button. No cache display.

L2.recipe: Read vs_ignis_prefix_cache, render top 5 as collapsible accordion with query + excerpt.

L3.recipe: Service Worker cache of last 3 full IGNIS responses (not just prefix excerpts), served from cache on network fail with 'From your last session' badge.

candidates.premiseEvidence: ignis-answer-engine.js:48 .catch returns empty docs silently; ignis-answer-engine.js:180 prefix cache exists and is read on hits — not on misses/errors

candidates.title: OG image uniqueness gate — no page references another page's OG image
candidates.why: check-og-images.mjs (S194) already validates that no page uses an SVG OG or points to a missing asset. But it does NOT check for cross-page OG reuse — one project page was found using og-image.png (the old generic fallback) which is not a bespoke card. A page that shares another page's OG image shows the wrong preview on social, damaging first-impression conversion from social traffic. This gate closes the 'page A's bespoke OG card appearing on page B' class AND catches leftover generic-fallback usages.
candidates.recipe: Extend check-og-images.mjs: (1) collect all og:image URL values across all tracked HTML pages; (2) flag any URL that appears on >1 page AND one of those pages is NOT the canonical owner of that image name; (3) flag any page using assets/og-image.png or assets/og/og-home.png outside of index.html. Wire into build:check as ERROR. Conversion outcome: every social share shows the right preview, not a recycled card.
candidates.evidence: grep og:image projects/ → 1 hit on legacy assets/og-image.png found; check-og-images.mjs confirmed present but only validates SVG+missing (head -20 output confirms); no cross-ref logic exists

L1.recipe: Grep for assets/og-image.png and assets/og/og-home.png outside index.html → ERROR if found.

L2.recipe: Full cross-ref in check-og-images.mjs: build og:image→pages[] map, flag any URL shared across multiple pages.

L3.recipe: Auto-generate missing bespoke OG cards for pages that currently use a generic fallback, using sharp (already a trusted devDep per S196) + SVG template.

candidates.premiseEvidence: grep og:image projects/ found 1 hit on assets/og-image.png (legacy fallback); check-og-images.mjs head -20 confirms no cross-ref check exists

candidates.title: Web push notifications — VAPID is READY, build the actual feature
candidates.why: VAPID keys are provisioned and READY (cloudflare.vapid 3/3 keys present, S207). push-dispatch.mjs scaffold exists. The actual feature — Worker subscribe endpoint + client opt-in UI + push send path — was deferred each session after S207 despite the credential being live. Shipping this converts the site from pull-only (visitors must return) to push-capable (the studio can bring visitors back). For a single-founder studio, push notifications on a new dispatch or project launch are high-leverage. Conversion outcome: direct subscriber re-engagement path.
candidates.recipe: Three parts: (1) Worker push endpoint: add /v/push-subscribe route to cloudflare/security-headers-worker.js — validates subscription object, stores in KV (cloudflare.kv capability); (2) client opt-in: assets/push-subscribe.js — calls navigator.serviceWorker.ready, subscribes with VAPID public key from api/build-sha.json sidecar, POSTs to /v/push-subscribe, stores vs_push_subscribed in localStorage; (3) push-dispatch.mjs --send sends a test push via web-push to stored subscriptions. Wire opt-in button into /vault-member/ dashboard.
candidates.evidence: cloudflare.vapid READY (3/3 keys); scripts/push-dispatch.mjs scaffold confirmed; grep 'push-subscribe' → 0 hits in worker confirms endpoint not yet built; grep 'pushManager\.subscribe' → 0 hits in assets confirms client not built

L1.recipe: Build api/build-sha.json with VAPID public key embedded. Wire push-subscribe.js minimal opt-in (button + localStorage flag). No server endpoint yet.

L2.recipe: Full Worker subscribe endpoint + client opt-in + push-dispatch.mjs --send test. Wired into /vault-member/ portal.

L3.recipe: Segment-aware push: dispatch:new triggers push to subscribed members; milestone push (N oracle queries, new game available) as retention signals. Topic subscription: members opt into specific content types.

candidates.premiseEvidence: check-secrets cloudflare.vapid → READY 3/3; push-dispatch.mjs scaffold exists; grep pushManager.subscribe assets/ → 0 hits; grep /v/push-subscribe worker.js → 0 hits

candidates.title: Derive nav Projects + Games dropdowns from api/public-intelligence.json
candidates.why: propagate-nav.mjs hardcodes the Games and Projects dropdown entries (lines 102-103). This broke twice (S208 found outdated links; S209 noted as deferred pending 'catalog∪extra-paged merge design'). api/public-intelligence.json (26KB, fresh 2026-06-19) already contains the canonical project + game list with status, URLs, and labels — it is the deployed source of truth for all public intelligence surfaces. Deriving the nav from it at build time (npm run propagate-nav reads public-intelligence.json) eliminates the drift class entirely. The 'catalog∪extra-paged merge' concern was about adding pages not in the catalog to the dropdown — we can handle that with an explicit EXTRA_NAV override list. Conversion outcome: nav always reflects live project state, no manual sync.
candidates.recipe: In scripts/propagate-nav.mjs: (1) read api/public-intelligence.json at the top of the script; (2) filter projects by status (SPARKED/FORGE/VAULTED) and type (game/project); (3) generate the dropdown HTML dynamically, grouping by status; (4) add EXTRA_NAV_ENTRIES = [] constant for pages not in the catalog (e.g. /games/vaultspark-forge/ scaffold pages); (5) add check-nav-catalog-sync.mjs gate that verifies the committed nav HTML matches what would be generated from the current catalog. Deferred concern resolved: extra-paged entries go in the EXTRA_NAV constant, not the catalog.
candidates.evidence: propagate-nav.mjs:102-103 hardcoded dropdown confirmed; api/public-intelligence.json fresh (26904 bytes, 2026-06-19); S209 honest deferral confirmed: 'needs catalog∪extra-paged merge design' — now resolved by EXTRA_NAV pattern

L1.recipe: Read public-intelligence.json, generate Games dropdown only (smaller surface). Manual verify before committing.

L2.recipe: Both Games + Projects dropdowns derived; EXTRA_NAV_ENTRIES constant; check-nav-catalog-sync.mjs gate wired into build:check.

L3.recipe: Full nav-from-catalog system: Universe dropdown too; automated CI verify that new catalog entries auto-appear within one build:check run; notify if a SPARKED project is missing a nav entry.

candidates.premiseEvidence: propagate-nav.mjs lines 102-103 hardcoded confirmed; api/public-intelligence.json 26904 bytes fresh; S208/S209 both documented the drift without fixing it
